summary: Windows and browser selection toolbars now soft-delete board roots and restore eligible roots from board Trash. Existing selection, confirmation, recovery transport and Rust lifecycle owners are reused. delete_selected_roots shares locked eligibility and revision rules with Archive; state changes, one board revision and a command-bound receipt commit atomically. Trash reads effective Deleted state separately from Archive under fresh selected-board access. Current Owner authorization is required for every write and receipt replay; uncertain saves recover through reads without resubmission.
evidence: Retry diagnosis on the live Windows/PostgreSQL fixture: --placement-move reached pending with one submission and visible feedback. In --placement-order, releasing root 67 before 61 also submitted exactly once, but the extra Trash button row pushed 'Saving item order…' to y=1110 below the 1095px viewport. The native test correctly timed out waiting for visible feedback. Archive and Trash now share one recovery row in MainTable::render_active. Temporary geometry diagnostics were removed; the original native assertions and timeout are unchanged.

After the layout fix, cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke -- windows_moves_and_reorders_single_roots --exact --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed (1/1, 24.38s), including pending duplicate suppression, saved order and fresh-process reopen. The same exact-case command for windows_deletes_and_restores_board_roots passed (1/1, 101.68s) on the same final sources and dedicated database. Full verification remains with the runner.

Source-backed expectations, not a newly executed comparison: reviewed the recorded toolbar-to-batch-operation and recovery-query trace underlying packets/36-browser-selection-group-move.md, 37-browser-root-archive-restore.md, 51-selected-root-archive.md and 52-board-item-trash.md. Delete confirms the original selection, sets each root's own Deleted state and increments revisions; recovery gives Deleted precedence over Archived and blocks roots in inactive groups. No fresh reference application comparison was executed. Trash Restore intentionally accepts only own Deleted roots in active groups, continuing the existing recovery-surface boundary rather than exposing the reference's arbitrary generic Restore.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke -- windows_archives_selected_roots windows_deletes_and_restores_board_roots --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed both focused cases. The Trash case exercised twelve isolated live Windows scenarios through actual Kit checkboxes, folding, toolbar, dialog, Escape/focus restoration, Tab/Enter confirmation, pending suppression, recovery controls and reload. Conflicts, unavailable original targets, deferred commit refusal, failed review/retry, demotion, lost membership/session and uncertain acknowledgment/refresh were checked against independent whole-store snapshots. The required Trash case also passed separately before the combined regression run.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --features browser-smoke --test browser_preview browser_deletes_and_restores_board_roots -- --exact --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed. Eleven isolated scenarios used owned headless Chromium profiles and real controls, capturing selected-board methods, paths, statuses, ordered targets, revisions and operation identity. Cancellation retained selection and focus, stale/refused saves retained original IDs for read/review/adoption, unavailable targets prevented adoption, permission/session loss was enforced, and uncertain saves recovered by GET without a second POST. Direct Trash-address reload and restore-one were exercised.

On both clients selection [67,59] survived cancellation and a folded g-20, then both roots left the active table atomically. At the checked baseline board/2 advanced to /3 once; both roots became Deleted/2. Trash listed [68,59,67] in physical order, while Archive retained only group-blocked 57. Restoring 67 alone produced Active/3 and board/4, returning it between 61 and 77 in g-90. Roots 59 and 68 stayed deleted. Independent new connections compared every item, board, group, field stamp, creation field, receipt and saved fold; unrelated archived, staging and foreign records were unchanged.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --test loopback_board_access selected_root_ -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed both selected_root_archive_is_atomic_and_authorized and required selected_root_trash_is_atomic_and_authorized. Real native bearer and matched preview requests used separate sessions. Checks covered empty/duplicate/nil/oversized input, the 10,000-target bound, stale board or one-item revision, foreign/missing/hidden/Archived/Deleted/Staging targets, refused deferred commit and competing commands with one winner. Exact replay changed nothing; order-only, revision, content, actor and operation-kind changes conflicted. Current role, board/workspace access, membership and session were enforced before replay. A one-root selection also deleted and replayed without affecting its neighbour.

The same Trash host case checked Member/Viewer recovery reads and denied restores on both transports, withdrawn read access, rejected sessions, stale restore, Archive/Trash command collisions and exact Delete replay after a later Restore without deleting again. Deleted and archived containing groups blocked item recovery. Effective group deletion included hidden roots without rewriting their own states. A 108-item inventory returned exactly 100 ordered items with has_more; restoring an unlisted target was refused without changing any record.

Upgrade checks migrated populated v11 and v12 fixtures twice, reconnected, preserved item records and replayed earlier single-root, selection-move and selected-Archive receipts. Reusing those identities for Delete conflicted. Migration 0013_root_trash.sql only extends receipt kinds/shapes; it does not rewrite prior receipts or content. cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --test loopback_board_access preview_root_lifecycle -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture also passed both inherited lifecycle authorization/visibility/replay cases and their older upgrade fixtures.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --features browser-smoke --test browser_preview browser_archives_ -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed all three focused regressions: single-root, group and selected-root Archive. Browser compilation retained the existing unused moved_root/reordered_root fixture-method warning.

Focused Clippy passed with -D warnings for board, client and host libraries, and for the desktop binary/windows_smoke target with native-smoke. cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed. Diff statistics and scope were inspected. The worker's documentation changes are only the affected Trash workflow row and this handoff. Pre-existing ROADMAP.md, scripts/run.mjs and packet edits were preserved; no gates or verification markers were changed.

Not run: full packet/workspace suites and Node runner verification, intentionally left for the runner's single full verification. The attempted runner-status command was denied by worker shell policy. No fresh reference runtime comparison, Android Trash UI, descendant storage, bulk restore, permanent deletion, group Trash recovery, search/paging UI, derived views, downstream effects or pixel/theme/zoom fidelity is claimed. No attended clipboard interaction, commit, push, publication or deployment was performed.
